root_idea.summary: The root has two principal semantic orientations: bearing or carrying a burden, and sound. Its carrying branch includes loads, pack animals, riding companions, and related figurative descriptions; its sound branch includes animal and bow sounds.
root_idea.development: The carrying orientation extends to the pack animal and to sharing or balancing a load, while weakness may be figured as becoming burden-like. The sound orientation remains a separate branch. Wrapping and being wrapped are directly attested in derived formations and in the Quranic form, but are not treated as the sole root principle.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested active participle is presented as its own normalized dictionary form.

senses.definition: One wrapped in his garment or garments.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participial epithet for a person who has wrapped himself in clothing; the Quranic occurrence is in 73:1.

senses.definition: By allusion, one wrapped up and remiss or slow to attend to the task before him.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quran-focused interpretation of 73:1 treats the physical wrapping metaphorically, as a kenning for inattention or reluctance rather than merely describing clothing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To run or go quickly with an appearance of limping or leaning to one side.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Described of people and animals, including horses and wild asses; the apparent limp may be associated with briskness, pride, or self-conceit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bear or carry a thing or load, taking it up or raising it onto the back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ordinary transitive carrying construction; the carried object may be a load.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone ride behind him, or to ride with him so as to counterbalance him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially a shared ride on a camel or in a howdah.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To follow another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive following construction, also reflected in the associated noun for a companion or follower.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wrap someone in a garment or garments.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II transitive usage, with the clothing expressed by a preposition or by a phrase meaning in his garments.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Concealment or the act of hiding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extension explicitly derived from wrapping.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The requiting of beneficence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional Form III noun distinct from the riding and balancing sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To recite or chant rajaz verse with one another, or to vie in doing so.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term زَمَل is used for the metre or verse type also called rajaz.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drive camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form Q.Q usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A load or burden; figuratively, a burden of knowledge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The knowledge sense is reported as a figurative use of the ordinary burden meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Household goods, furniture, or utensils.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use referring to household belongings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A half.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the idiom مَا فِي جُوَالِكَ إِلَّا زِمْلٌ, ‘there is only a half in your sack’; the evidence does not establish a broader unrestricted sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of verse or poetry, especially rajaz.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may be contrasted with or confused with رَمَل in a reported variant reading, while both are said to agree in meaning in the cited verse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A company or group of persons travelling together, or a collection in general.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The travel-companion sense is especially associated with people journeying together; some authorities extend it to any company or collection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dense or abundant growth or cluster, especially of palms or young palm shoots.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to luxuriant dense palms, a collection of young shoots, or young palms exceeding the reach of the hand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wrapper placed over a leather water-skin or water-bag.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is also reported in forms referring to several such wrappers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A riding or travelling companion, especially one who rides behind another or shares a mount or howdah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word extends to a companion who assists another in his affairs and to two people working together with their camels; it can also be used figuratively for an assistant in an intellectual undertaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cowardly, weak, low, mean, or contemptible person who withdraws into his house or tent instead of rising to difficult action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description includes indolent refraining from warfare or from aspiring to great things; this Classical specialization is kept separate from the Quranic participle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel or other beast used to carry a traveller’s goods, household belongings, and provisions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually a she-camel or other pack animal; the plural is زَوَامِلُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A half-load containing a pilgrim’s travelling provisions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later specialized use for the portion of a load containing dry bread, dates, and similar provisions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Camels bearing their loads.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective or plural-like use for loaded camels or a laden caravan.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A knower of an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Restricted to the reported idiomatic expression هو ابن زوملتها, referring to someone thoroughly acquainted with the matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The son of a female slave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate reported idiom, not a general meaning of زَوْمَلَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sound or noise, including a mixed or confused sound, the sound of a horse’s prepuce, or the twanging of a bow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The bow sense is attested in the plural expression أَزَامِيلُ القِسِيِّ; the listed applications are varieties of the sound branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A family or household together with its cattle or other property; by extension, numerous families or households.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions for leaving one’s family behind or setting out with one’s whole household and livestock.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take a thing altogether, including its furniture or utensils.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed expression emphasizing the taking of the whole of something and its associated belongings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A shoemaker’s knife used to cut leather.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized implement sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A crescent-shaped iron attached to the end of a spear for catching wild oxen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate hunting implement sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The implement called مِطْرَقَة, a mallet or hammering tool.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical implement sense reported under the same headword as the shoemaker’s knife.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Figuratively of a man, a great or vehement eater or a strong man; also, contrariwise, a weak, low, or contemptible man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence explicitly preserves opposite evaluations under this figurative application rather than resolving them into one value.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vociferous animal, especially a mountain goat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form and its reported variant إِزْمَوْلٌ may be applied to a mountain goat or another animal making a loud noise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wrapped vessel used for cooling and dispensing water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Iraqi vessel, traditionally wrapped with cloth and straw so that the water remains cool.

cautions: The public headword is normalized to the indefinite active-participle citation form مُزَّمِّلٌ, while the supplied Quran occurrence is definite and inflected.
The figurative implication of remissness in the second Quranic sense is an interpretive reading of the physical wrapping; the supplied discussion also records a gentling or mollifying interpretation.
Some Classical entries preserve expressly contrary evaluations, such as strong or voracious versus weak or contemptible; these have been retained rather than harmonized.
